title: ΛCDM as a Special Case of Energy-Flow Cosmology: Regime Structure, Empirical Confrontation, and the Limits of Background-Level Testing
description: Presents Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC) as a unified framework in which ΛCDM arises as the special-case limit in the linear, homogeneous, high-density regime (L0/L1), derived directly from the EFC variational action. Using DESI DR2, the background coupling α = −0.14 ± 0.21 is found consistent with ΛCDM, while the paper delineates testable beyond-ΛCDM predictions in L2/L3 including a perturbation-sector survival valley, a universal screening parameter for rotation curves, and a deep-void ISW sign-flip.

regime_driver.description: Dimensionless entropy-gradient intensity that drives regime classification; large χ indicates strong-gradient (nonlinear) behavior.

constitutive_law.description: Material (transport) response of the energy-flow field to entropy gradients; κ(χ) encodes regime-dependent conductivity.

modified_poisson.description: EFC-modified Poisson equation with an effective gravitational coupling μ controlling deviations from GR in structure growth.

effective_mu.description: Scale- and regime-dependent enhancement/suppression of gravity, with ε(k) anchored by the discrete gravity sector and F(χ) an activation function.

relativistic_action.latex: S_{\rm EFC} = \int d^4x \, \sqrt{-g} \, \left[ \frac{F(\phi)}{2} R - \frac{K(\rho)}{2} (\nabla \phi)^2 - V(\phi) + \lambda \, C[\phi, \nabla \phi] + S_m \right]
relativistic_action.description: Variational action coupling an entropy-flow scalar to curvature with density-dependent stiffness and a flow constraint; yields μ, Σ, η dynamics with c_T = c.

lcdm_limit.description: Formal reduction showing ΛCDM as the L0/L1 limit: high density, early/linear regime, and strong acceleration suppress all EFC corrections.

key_results.main_finding: ΛCDM is recovered as the exact special-case limit of EFC in L0/L1, and DESI DR2 yields α = −0.14 ± 0.21 (0.65σ from null), consistent with ΛCDM in the background sector.

sealed_predictions.statement: Deep cosmic voids (δ ≲ −0.8) produce an ISW temperature sign-flip relative to ΛCDM.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Stacked CMB–void cross-correlation using DESI/SDSS void catalogs and Planck/Simons Observatory maps.

sealed_predictions.statement: A narrow perturbation-sector survival valley with μ ≈ 0.93–0.96, Σ ≈ 1.03–1.07, and η ≠ 1 (≈1.10) at intermediate scales.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Joint weak-lensing + galaxy clustering + RSD tomography (e.g., DESI, KiDS, HSC, LSST, Euclid) measuring {μ, Σ, η} across 0.1 < k < 0.5 h Mpc⁻¹ and 0.3 < z < 1.

sealed_predictions.statement: Galaxy rotation curves can be fit without particle dark matter using a single universal screening parameter k ≈ 0.415 ± 0.029.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: High-precision rotation curves for new, homogeneous samples (SPARC-like) testing the universality and predicted scatter of k.

kill_criteria: KC1: No ISW sign-flip detected for deep voids (δ ≤ −0.8) at >5σ in stacked CMB–void analyses over 50–200 h⁻¹ Mpc scales would falsify EFC’s gradient-driven regime behavior.

KC2: Stage-IV joint analyses constrain μ = 1.00 ± 0.01, Σ = 1.00 ± 0.02, and η = 1.00 ± 0.02 across 0.1 < k < 0.5 h Mpc⁻¹ and 0.3 < z < 0.8, excluding the survival valley (μ ≈ 0.94, Σ ≈ 1.05, η ≈ 1.10) at >5σ, thereby falsifying the perturbation-sector mechanism.

KC3: A large, homogeneous SPARC-quality sample cannot be fit with a single universal k (post-systematics intrinsic scatter > 25%) or yields ΔAIC > 50 in favor of CDM/NFW over EFC’s screening model, falsifying the discrete gravity/screening sector.
KC4: Failure of exact GR recovery in the Solar System (e.g., measured |γ − 1| > 1e−5 or |β − 1| > 1e−5 attributable to EFC corrections) would falsify the L3 limit of the theory.
KC5: Independent laboratory/astrophysical bounds require ε(k→0) far below the Graph-AQUAL anchor (e.g., ε(k→0) ≪ C^2 − 1 ≈ 4.4), incompatible with the amplitude needed for EFC’s L2 phenomenology.
short_title: ΛCDM as Special Case of EFC
abstract: Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC) treats the universe as a continuous energy-flow system governed by entropy gradients. This paper demonstrates that the standard ΛCDM model arises as the special-case limit of EFC in the linear, homogeneous, high-density regime (L0/L1), analogous to the ideal gas law emerging from statistical mechanics. DESI DR2 multi-probe analysis confirms this limit empirically: α = −0.14 ± 0.21 (0.65σ from null). Beyond L0/L1, EFC produces testable predictions that ΛCDM does not.
